items.title: The Ghost in the Grip: The Science of Slip and Why Early Detection is Central to Robotic Dexterity
items.summary: Slip is not a sudden failure; it begins as a subtle, measurable change at the contact interface before an object visibly moves. This post explores the physics of incipient slip, why humans can correct a slipping grasp before conscious thought, and what robotic tactile systems must sense to do the same. It explains why dexterous machines need both fast dynamic sensing and slower spatial force/pressure mapping, and why the future of robotic grip control depends on feeling earlier rather than gripping harder.
